BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.

To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and
look forward to your mark-up.

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims
is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.
Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and
only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the
basket is recoverable.
Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after
Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims
unless expressly stated otherwise.
Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same
caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.
Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and
non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

registers (see Disclosure Letter).
Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the

public records.

records are fictional.
1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the
indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including
DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly
searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific
disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent,
payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2.
As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security
is included.
4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of

Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or

loss amount.

Buyer has completed its own verification.

must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel — Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Internal / privileged. Seller material treated as adversarial drafting, not agreed positions.

## Headline

The Seller's package is not "fair and balanced" — it departs from our playbook on almost every liability and risk-allocation point, and the Disclosure Letter itself confirms that the key completion deliverables (Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, Ironquay assignment, independent title evidence) **do not yet exist**. Several Seller positions silently assume fallbacks that Amelia Frost has not authorised. Nothing here should be treated as agreed.

---

## 1. Liability regime — reject in full

| Point | Seller draft | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (cl 12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m; 20% only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority (none given) | Seller has written our *unauthorised fallback* in as the "negotiated" position. Revert to 25%. Do not accept 20% in any mark-up absent written sign-off identifying the draft. |
| De minimis (cl 12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5× our position. Reject. |
| Basket (cl 12.2) | AUD 250,000, **excess-only** (deductible) | AUD 50,000, **first-dollar** (tipping) | 5× our figure *and* a change of basket type. The deductible structure alone shifts AUD 250k of risk to us. Reject both. |
| Claims period (cl 12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months; 18 months only with Amelia Frost written approval (none given) | Same pattern as the cap — Seller has assumed our fallback. Revert to 24 months. |
| "All limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated" (cl 12.3/13) | Blanket override | Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override | This is the single most dangerous drafting device in the package. It would sweep Fundamental, Tax, IP, specific indemnities and covenant claims into the 20%/18-month regime by default. Delete. Replace with the reverse rule: limitations apply **only** to General Warranty Claims unless expressly extended. |

## 2. Fundamental / Title warranties — reject

Seller proposes capacity and title warranties sit under the general cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity." That is a substantive transfer of the core deal risk, not an admin point. Require the playbook regime: **separate cap at 100% of price, minimum six years, outside de minimis, basket and any knowledge bar.** "Administrative simplicity" is not a consideration we should accept for the warranty that we actually own what we are paying AUD 24m for.

## 3. Fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct — missing entirely

Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 apply the limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions to "all Claims of any nature." There is **no fraud carve-out anywhere in the Seller's package**. This is a hard line: fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of every cap, basket, time limit, exclusive remedy and non-reliance clause to the maximum extent enforceable. Nobody on our side has authority to waive this. Insert the carve-out expressly in 9.3, 12 and 20.5.

## 4. Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter §1) — reject general disclosure

Paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2 purport to disclose "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records." This is whole-data-room plus public-register deemed disclosure — exactly what the playbook rejects. Require the standard of **specific, fair disclosure** (sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter) and delete 1.1/1.2 as general disclosures. Para 1.4 (no admissions) is acceptable only once the general disclosure is removed; otherwise it compounds the problem by disclosing everything while admitting nothing.

Note the Seller's own numbered disclosures (§§2–10) are actually quite candid — see Part 7 below — and in several places undercut the Seller's "Update" positions. Use them.

## 5. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) — delete

Seller bars any claim where "the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records." Combined with §1.1/1.2 this would effectively eliminate the warranty package: anything in the data room is both "disclosed" and "known." Delete 8.3. If any knowledge qualifier survives negotiation, it must be (a) limited to the **actual knowledge of named seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry** (i.e. a seller-side qualifier on warranties, not a buyer-side bar on claims), and (b) never apply to title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

## 6. Completion-critical deliverables

### Bluefen (cl 3 / 6.3)
- Seller: reasonable endeavours; consent "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent."
- Disclosure §2 confirms: ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30% of revenue); change-control cl 11.2 with **conditions in 11.3**; **no final written consent and no evidence the 11.3 conditions are satisfied.**
- Position: this is a material customer at ~30% of revenue. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient. The condition precedent must require (i) an **effective** consent in a form acceptable to us, **and** (ii) evidence that every 11.3 condition is satisfied, **before Completion**. "Consent-on-delivery" is rejected — a conditional consent whose conditions are unmet is not consent.

### Riverlark (cl 2 / 7)
- Seller: ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion."
- Disclosure §3 confirms: not repaid; no final discharge of security; change-control cl 8.1 and discharge cl 9.2 engaged.
- Position: this is a debt-free/cash-free deal. Require a **current payout figure**, **direct repayment to Riverlark out of Completion funds**, and **effective security releases (incl. PPSR discharges) at Completion**. A post-completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable bank undertaking *and* Amelia Frost's approval — neither is on the table. Also flag that the change-of-control provision in 8.1 may itself be a default trigger if not dealt with pre-Completion.

### Title (DD-012)
- Seller: title is "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012."
- Disclosure §10 concedes the register merely "identifies the source relied on" and that we have not completed our own verification.
- Position: a company's own register is a seller-supplied internal document, not independent proof. Require independent evidence of ownership, absence of encumbrances (ASIC extract, PPSR, constitution, pre-emptive rights waivers, board minutes), and seller authority. Combined with Part 2, title must sit in the Fundamental regime.

## 7. Specific commercial / indemnity items

### Employee bonuses (DD-005 — AUD 420,000)
Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised. Disclosure §5 confirms they are **absent from the funds flow** and on-costs (payroll tax, super) are unaddressed. Risk: the obligation sits in the Company (which we are buying), so post-Completion *we* fund it unless the price mechanics catch it. Require either (a) a specific line item in the funds flow treating AUD 420,000 **plus triggered on-costs** as a deduction/Debt-like item, or (b) seller-funded with evidence of payment. "Not separately itemised" is precisely the silent exclusion the playbook prohibits.

### Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)
Seller limits the indemnity to the SOW3 payment and calls it "adequate." Disclosure §4 confirms cl 7.3 conditions **transfer of SOW3 Project Materials** on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open (not independently verified); **no receipt or confirmatory assignment exists**. The real exposure is not the AUD 180k — it is that the Company may not own the SOW3 IP. Broaden the indemnity to cover loss arising from any failure of title to the SOW3 (and related) Project Materials, third-party claims, and remediation cost, while preserving the cure path (pay SOW3 fees pre-Completion → obtain confirmatory assignment). Treat the AUD 180,000 as unverified in either direction and seek bank confirmation.

### Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
Seller: "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material." Disclosure §6: link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps); unknown whether accessed; notification need undetermined. Consistent with the playbook, we **do not** assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or any number. But "not expected to be material" is a conclusion the Seller's own disclosure does not support. Require: log preservation, completion of the investigation, pre-Completion update covenant, specific warranty on the facts, and a specific indemnity sitting outside the general regime for loss arising from the incident (including any regulatory notification determined to be required).

### Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011 — AUD 330,000)
Seller: ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure §8 says the material does not establish whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. Playbook: assess, no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. Agreed — but push for information (terms, termination rights, accrual position, whether already in the FY26 numbers) before accepting the "ordinary course" label.

### Office lease (DD-007) / Mossvale (DD-009)
Seller's disclosures say notification (lease) and assignment restriction (Mossvale) do not amount to share-sale consents. Plausible, but confirm against the documents; add a pre-Completion covenant to give any required notices.

## 8. Tax / IP — not settled

Seller declares tax and IP "settled under the general regime above." They are not. Playbook: these remain **OPEN**, must be kept as separate categories, with no unlimited liability assumed and no resolution assumed. Reject the characterisation and ensure the cl 12.3/13 override (Part 1) cannot be used to backdoor them into the 20%/18-month regime.

---

## Summary of recommendations

**Reject outright (no authority to accept):**
1. 20% / AUD 4.8m cap → revert to 25% / AUD 6.0m.
2. 18-month claims period → revert to 24 months.
3. Absence of any fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve-out → insert across 9.3, 12, 20.5.
4. "All limitations apply to all Claims" default → reverse it.
5. Fundamental/Title under general caps → separate 100% / six-year regime, outside thresholds and knowledge bar.

**Reject and re-draft:**
6. De minimis AUD 25k → AUD 5k; basket AUD 250k deductible → AUD 50k tipping.
7. General data-room / public-register disclosure (§1.1–1.2) → specific fair disclosure only.
8. Clause 8.3 buyer-knowledge bar → delete; any residual qualifier is seller-knowledge, named persons, reasonable enquiry, never title/capacity/fraud/specific indemnities.

**Completion mechanics:**
9. Bluefen: effective consent + evidence 11.3 conditions satisfied, pre-Completion CP; no consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours insufficient.
10. Riverlark: current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion.
11. Funds flow: DD-005 bonuses AUD 420k + on-costs as a specific line item or seller-funded.
12. Title: independent ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is not sufficient.

**Specific risk items:**
13. Ironquay: broaden indemnity to IP ownership failure; preserve SOW3 payment/assignment cure; verify the AUD 180k.
14. DD-006: preservation, investigation, update covenant, specific warranty and indemnity outside general regime; no assumed breach or quantum.
15. Sandbar: information request before accepting ordinary-course treatment; no automatic Debt deduction.
16. Tax/IP: record as OPEN; resist "settled."

**Process note:** the Seller has twice written our *unauthorised* fallbacks (20% cap, 18 months) into its draft as if negotiated. Our mark-up and cover note should state expressly that nothing in the Seller Update is agreed and that the Buyer's positions remain as previously communicated, to avoid any later argument that silence on those points was acceptance. Any movement toward the fallbacks requires Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the specific draft.
